The use of SDF in ACT NW verification would require the following enhancements: • Spatial regularizations to extract radiation sources of relevant shapes and sizes during source field reconstruction; • Counting of reconstructed sources, especially when noisy; • Model-selection / hypothesis testing methods for counting sources; • Design of most informative paths for any autonomous SDF platform (design of experiments); and • Stable operation without human interaction (i.e., fully autonomous operation) thus leading to simplified implementations of information barriers. 4.5.2 Nuclear Compliance Verification The NCV mission comprises multiple teams with complimentary scope. The primary teams are scoped with Plutonium and Uranium production andweaponization; calledthePlutoniumVerificationTeam(PVT)andUraniumVerificationTeam (PVT), respectively. The Health and Safety Team (HST) is tasked with ensuring other teams’ members are safe while conducting their activities. A Test Site Verification Team (TSVT), whose tasking would comprise ensuring weapons testing sites comply with treaty obligations, has also been initiated. Anotherimportant aspect of the SDF technology for the HST members is the ability to export and manipulate data and SDF-derived data products. HST members are responsible for ensuring the safety of other teams, but those in other teams may insist upon detailed information such that they can make a well-informed assessment of the risk they are incurring. Also, many of the opportunities for R&D needs identified by HST members would also benefit other NCV teams as well as missions beyond NCV. The PVT is tasked with verification of all treaty compliance measures related to plutonium weapons and tritium production. The PVT’s mission is considering leveraging SDF technologies for radioactive source localization and characterization and would most directly benefit from LBNL Report #2001653 development of coupling neutron detection, localization, spectroscopy and multiplicity with SDF. Some of this work is underway with NA-22 Object J support and during this study, SDF systems have been part of PVT training exercises. Abilities to identify and characterize hold-up would be valuable as would the ability to automate methods of verifying that a facility has not been subject to further activities subsequent to an agreed-upon “freeze” and baselining inspection.
